controller_actions.task: Rewrite module.py so that solve(data) implements the user contract exactly. Apply data['ops'] in order. Keep balance, held, and a dict of active holds keyed by id. For each operation, in order: (1) kind must be credit, debit, hold, or release, else raise ValueError. (2) For credit, debit, hold, amount must be an int, not a bool, and at least 1, else raise ValueError. (3) For hold, id must not name an active hold; for release, id must name an active hold; otherwise raise ValueError. (4) For debit and hold, amount must not exceed available (balance minus held), else raise ValueError. Effects: credit adds amount to balance; debit subtracts amount from balance; hold adds amount to held and records the hold under id; release removes the hold named by id, subtracts its amount from held, and ignores any amount field. Return {'balance': balance, 'held': held, 'available': balance - held}. An empty ops list returns zeros. Do not mutate the input. Use only the Python standard library; no I/O and no dynamic code execution. Write only module.py.

Write test_cases.json for solve(data) in module.py, following the user contract exactly. It must be a JSON list of at least four distinct cases. Each case has an "input" object and exactly one of "output" (the expected result dict with balance, held, available) or "error" (the exception class name, e.g. "ValueError"). Cover: empty ops returning zeros; credit then debit; hold reducing available; release restoring available and ignoring its amount field; a debit exceeding available raising ValueError; a duplicate hold id raising ValueError; releasing an unknown id raising ValueError; a boolean amount raising ValueError; an unknown kind raising ValueError. Verify each expected value by hand against the contract. Write only test_cases.json.
